problem: Six stacked cards all answered 'how did I sleep' in a different form (score card, hypnogram, three-night outlook, 7/14/30 compare, and an AI card holding a settings table, a 7-night table, two charts, a ledger, reasoning, an outcome strip, two buttons and a live-nudge list). The reader could not tell at a glance how they slept or what the system was doing about it.
consulted: motion-canon CANON.md §10 (progressive disclosure, labelled nav, three-exit modals)

glanceHierarchy.question: I am in the bed right now and it is wrong
glanceHierarchy.answer: A live control above everything else: one reading, a big minus and a big plus, half a degree per press, held for the rest of the night. The press IS the comfort report — direction says which way it is wrong and the schedule already knows which stage is running, so nobody has to pick a word at 03:00. Collapses to a single line of text when the bed is off, so it does not compete during the day.
glanceHierarchy.why: Adjusting the bed in the night previously meant opening the folded schedule panel, identifying which of four stages was running, and editing it half asleep — or answering the morning prompt with words that describe the problem instead of fixing it. The guest share page already had a live control; the owner's own app did not.

glanceHierarchy.question: How did I sleep?
glanceHierarchy.answer: One hero card. Quality score ring, a plain-language HEADLINE naming what stood out ('Deep sleep was strong', 'A restless night'), and one sentence of detail comparing the night with the recent average. The overall score is demoted to a footnote because it is mostly duration and bedtime, which the bed does not control.
glanceHierarchy.budget: 1 number, 1 headline, 1 sentence, 1 stage bar, 4 vitals tiles

glanceHierarchy.question: What is being done about it?
glanceHierarchy.answer: A single-line status strip directly beneath the hero, stating tonight's change in words ('the REM stage runs cooler, 28.8 → 27.8. Live on the pod'), or that nothing changed and why. Tapping it expands the full autopilot detail.

glanceHierarchy.question: Show me the night / the trend
glanceHierarchy.answer: One Trends card with three tabs: Night (hypnogram + temperature + events), Recent (last two nights vs tonight's forecast), Compare (7/14/30 days). Replaces three separate cards.
glanceHierarchy.budget: one card, one active panel at a time

glanceHierarchy.question: Why did it decide that? What has it tried?
glanceHierarchy.answer: Behind the autopilot strip: plan comparison, per-stage reasoning, evidence, expectation, principle, experiment ledger, settings history.

glanceHierarchy.question: Change my settings
glanceHierarchy.answer: Collapsed disclosures at the foot of the page: schedule, autopilot settings.

densityBudget.rule: No card may hold more than one job. The AI card held ten and is now a level-3 panel behind a level-1 line.

colour.var(--success): quality >= 80, a change that helped, converged
colour.var(--warning): quality 65-79, waiting on the user, no assessment yet
colour.var(--warm): a warmer temperature / measured bed temperature
colour.var(--accent): tonight, the current selection, the app's own actions

semanticContract.rule: Colour never carries meaning alone: every status pairs with a word (the verdict headline, the change column, the chip label) and, where it is an affordance, a Grunkicon glyph.

disclosureLedger.content: two nights ago / last night / tonight forecast
plan curve, stage comparison, reasoning, evidence, ledger, settings history, live nudges

disclosureLedger.now: nested disclosure inside the autopilot panel

motion.tabSwitch: --motion-fast with --ease-out-snap, no layout jump: the panel is keyed so content cross-fades
motion.stripExpand: grid-template-rows 0fr→1fr at --motion-base, matching the existing disclosures
motion.reducedMotion: inherits the global gate in globals.css
